comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C72-C79 regarding the CD81+ fibroblast-C3-neutrophil axis in the LIP mouse model. Both evaluations find the evidence solid and affirm that the mouse model validates the human findings.

Strong agreement on claims C60-C71 regarding the C3/C3aR1 pathway mediating CD81+ fibroblast-neutrophil interactions. Both evaluations describe the evidence as solid, with OpenEval noting validation across multiple experimental approaches and peer reviewers explicitly affirming the mechanism.

Strong agreement on claims C50-C59 regarding CD81+ fibroblasts' pro-inflammatory metabolic activity and SASP characteristics. Both evaluations find solid evidence, though OpenEval provides more detailed assessment of the bioinformatics analyses while peer reviewers focus on the overall inflammatory contribution.

Strong agreement on claims C42-C49 regarding CD81 as a marker of senescent fibroblasts with high SASP enrichment. Both evaluations describe the evidence as solid and affirm the identification of CD81+ fibroblasts as a key senescent subpopulation.

Strong agreement on claims C80-C86 regarding ABT263 (Navitoclax) senolytic treatment alleviating periodontitis. Both evaluations find the evidence solid and describe this as a significant improvement. OpenEval notes the lack of micro-CT data for bone loss confirmation, while peer reviewers do not mention this limitation.

Strong agreement on claims C33-C41 regarding fibroblasts as the main senescent cell population in periodontitis. Both evaluations affirm the scRNA-seq evidence and find it solid, with peer reviewers explicitly confirming fibroblasts are enriched for senescence markers.

Strong agreement on claims C18-C32 regarding increased cellular senescence in the LIP model and human samples. Both evaluations describe the evidence as solid, combining in vitro and in vivo analyses. Peer review R1 also includes claims C15-C17 and C100, showing broader grouping of senescence findings.

Agreement on claims C15-C17 regarding increased senescence markers in human periodontitis samples. OpenEval finds SA-β-gal and IHC data clearly demonstrate the findings, while peer reviewers group these with broader senescence evidence (C18-C32, C100) and describe the combined evidence as solid.

Agreement on claims C89-C95 regarding metformin's therapeutic effects through inhibition of cellular senescence. Both evaluations find solid evidence. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of multiple experimental approaches, while peer reviewers note this as a significant improvement to the manuscript.

Agreement on claims C96-C99 regarding in vitro mechanistic support for metformin's effects. OpenEval finds the data support direct effects on fibroblast senescence and the CD81-C3 axis. Peer review R8 groups these with broader metformin findings (C87-C95, C107) and describes the combined evidence as solid.

Agreement on claims C87-C88 regarding metformin's established senomorphic effects from prior literature. OpenEval finds these appropriately contextualize the novelty of investigating metformin in periodontitis. Peer review R8 groups these with the full metformin experimental findings (C89-C99, C107).

Agreement on claims C1-C4 regarding epidemiological background of periodontitis. OpenEval explicitly evaluates these as appropriately supported by citations. Peer review R10 implicitly accepts these background claims without explicit discussion, grouping them with broader contextual statements (C5-C14, C30).

Agreement on claims C5-C14 regarding cellular senescence biological background. OpenEval finds these well-supported by literature citations providing appropriate context. Peer review R10 implicitly accepts these as standard background statements without explicit discussion, focusing evaluation on novel experimental findings.

Agreement on claim C108 regarding CD81 as a potential therapeutic target. OpenEval finds this speculative and notes it would require functional validation (knockout/blocking experiments). Peer reviewers accept this as a suggestion rather than definitive proof, noting the therapeutic validation with ABT263 and metformin provides supporting evidence.

Agreement on claim C100 regarding overall conclusion that senescent cells accumulate in periodontitis. OpenEval finds this well-supported by comprehensive data. Peer review R1 groups this with the primary senescence evidence (C15-C32) and confirms the finding.

Partial disagreement on claims C101-C102 regarding fibroblast senescence role. OpenEval notes C102 (that senescence 'helps mitigate tissue damage') appears contradictory to overall findings and lacks direct support. Peer review R2 groups these with fibroblast senescence findings (C33-C41) and describes evidence as solid without noting the contradiction.

Agreement on claim C103 regarding CD81+ fibroblasts as a senescent subpopulation. OpenEval finds this well-supported by comprehensive data. Peer review R3 groups this with CD81 marker identification (C42-C49) and describes evidence as solid.

Agreement on claim C104 regarding CD81+ fibroblasts' pro-inflammatory characteristics. OpenEval finds this well-supported by comprehensive data. Peer review R4 groups this with SASP and metabolic findings (C50-C59) and describes evidence as solid.

Agreement on claim C105 regarding the C3/C3aR1 axis mechanism. OpenEval finds this well-supported by comprehensive data. Peer review R5 groups this with the full C3/C3aR1 pathway findings (C60-C71) and describes evidence as solid.

Agreement on claim C106 regarding senolytic therapy potential. OpenEval finds this well-supported but notes lack of micro-CT data. Peer review R7 groups this with ABT263 findings (C80-C86) and describes evidence as solid without noting the micro-CT limitation.

Agreement on claim C107 regarding metformin's therapeutic potential. OpenEval finds this well-supported by comprehensive data. Peer review R8 groups this with full metformin findings (C87-C99) and describes evidence as solid, noting it as a significant manuscript improvement.

Divergent evaluation on claim C27 regarding mitochondrial dysfunction. OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting it is inferred from pathway analysis without direct experimental validation. Peer review R1 groups this with broader senescence evidence (C15-C32, C100) and describes the combined evidence as solid without distinguishing correlative from causative findings.

Divergent evaluation on claim C52 regarding lipid metabolism upregulation. OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting it lacks direct experimental validation beyond correlative pathway analysis. Peer review R4 groups this with CD81+ fibroblast characteristics (C50-C59, C104) and describes evidence as solid without noting the need for functional validation.

Agreement on claim C30 regarding cGAS-STING pathway's established role. OpenEval finds this appropriately supported by literature citations providing context. Peer review R10 implicitly accepts this as standard background without explicit discussion.

Agreement on claim C53 regarding arachidonic acid metabolism biochemistry. OpenEval finds this appropriately supported by citation and metabolic pathway diagram. Peer review R4 groups this with CD81+ fibroblast metabolic findings (C50-C59, C104) without separate discussion of the biochemical background.

Agreement on claim C63 regarding C3/C3aR1 axis's established role in inflammation. OpenEval finds this appropriately supported by literature citations providing context. Peer review R5 groups this with the full C3/C3aR1 pathway findings (C60-C71, C105) without separate discussion of the background literature.
